title: Maximum bipartite matching: one augmenting path per vertex (Kuhn) vs Hopcroft-Karp
problem_statement: Given a bipartite graph with left vertices 0..n_left-1, right vertices 0..n_right-1 and edges given as adjacency lists of the left vertices, compute the maximum number of edges in a matching (a set of edges no two of which share a vertex).

input.parameter: n = V = n_left + n_right, the number of vertices; E denotes the number of edges.
input.size_measure: V + E (adjacency lists). Index operations are unit cost.

algorithms.name: Kuhn's augmenting paths (one DFS per left vertex)
algorithms.idea: For each left vertex in turn, search depth-first for an augmenting path (alternating between non-matching and matching edges, ending at a free right vertex) and flip it if found.
algorithms.pseudocode: for u in left: seen = {}; if dfs(u) finds a free right vertex along an alternating path: flip the path
algorithms.time_complexity: O(V (V + E)), i.e. O(V E) when E = Omega(V): one O(V + E) search per left vertex, and at most n_left E <= V E edge scans on every input (in one search a left vertex is pushed at most once, since the root is free and every other pushed vertex is the partner of a right vertex seen for the first time, and a pushed vertex reads each entry of its list at most once). On the adversarial family G_k (V = 4k^2 + k, E = 2k^4 + k^2) exactly (7k^6 + 9k^4 + 11k^2 - 3k)/6 edge scans for every k >= 1. Proof sketch, with a = k^2: before gadget root u < a, gadget left vertex i is matched to right vertex u - 1 - i (i < u), so the search from u runs through all u matched gadget vertices, reads (u + 1)(u + 2)/2 entries and succeeds; each of the other a gadget roots fails after reading a(a + 1) entries (its own list and the lists of the a matched gadget vertices); in path j the roots L_2..L_j read 1 entry each and L_1 reads 2j - 1, so path j costs 3j - 2. The sum C(a + 2, 3) + a^2 (a + 1) + k(3k - 1)/2 is the formula, and it equals the V2 counts listed under verification. So Kuhn makes Theta(V E) = Theta(V^3) scans on G_k; the ratio to V E tends to 7/48 (complete proofs: PROOFS.md sections 1, 2, 8 and 9)
algorithms.space_complexity: O(V): at most 4 n_left + 3 n_right list entries besides the input at any time, and at most 3 n_left + 2 n_right in the lists bound to local variables between statements (one word per entry; CPython's over-allocation of lists and its integer objects are not counted; PROOFS.md section 10)
algorithms.correctness: A matching is maximum iff it has no augmenting path (PROOFS.md section 5; credit: Berge 1957). When the search from u fails, no augmenting path starts at u for the current matching. That stays true after later augmentations. Proof: let P be the next augmenting path, from a free left vertex x != u to a free right vertex y (so u is not on P), and suppose that afterwards Q is an augmenting path from u. If Q avoids P, it was augmenting before. Otherwise let z be the first vertex of Q on P. The edge of Q entering z is not on P, and after the flip every vertex of P is matched by an edge of P, so that edge is unmatched and z is a right vertex. Then Q up to z, followed by P from z to y (which begins with the edge matching z before the flip, unless z = y), was an augmenting path from u before the flip: a contradiction. By induction the same holds after every later augmentation, so after all left vertices have been tried, no augmenting path exists. Complete proof (the stack is an alternating path, a failed search excludes every augmenting path from its root, the flip, the persistence argument above, and the direction of Berge's criterion that is used): PROOFS.md sections 5-6.

algorithms.name: Hopcroft-Karp
algorithms.idea: Work in phases. Each phase finds the length of a shortest augmenting path by BFS from all free left vertices, then augments along a maximal set of vertex-disjoint shortest augmenting paths found by DFS in the layered graph. The shortest length grows every phase.
algorithms.pseudocode: repeat: BFS layers from free left vertices (stop at the first layer with a free right vertex); if none: stop; DFS from each free left vertex along layer-increasing edges, removing dead ends and used paths; augment
algorithms.time_complexity: O((V + E) sqrt(V)): fewer than sqrt(2V) + 1 phases for V >= 1, O(V + E) each (PROOFS.md section 7, Theorem HK; credit: Hopcroft & Karp 1973); O(V^2.5) on dense graphs (the paper's title bound). On the adversarial family G_k exactly k + 1 phases (k augmenting phases and a final search that finds no augmenting path) and (24k^5 + 9k^4 + 4k^3 + 24k^2 - 25k + 12)/6 = Theta(E sqrt V) edge scans for every k >= 1; the ratio to E sqrt V tends to 1. Proof sketch, with a = k^2: in phase 1 the breadth-first search reads all E entries, and the depth-first searches read a(a + 1)/2 + a^2 + k(k + 1)/2 entries, match all a gadget right vertices and path 1, and leave path j >= 2 with the j - 1 edges L_i R_(i-1) matched and L_1, R_j free; in phase t (2 <= t <= k) the target level is t, the breadth-first search reads 2a^2 entries in the gadget and 2t - 1 in each path j >= t, and the depth-first searches read 2a^2 in the gadget, 2t - 1 in path t, which they repair, and 2t + 1 in each later path, which they leave unchanged; phase k + 1 reads 2a^2 entries and finds no free right vertex. The per-phase counts sum to the formula, which equals the V2 counts listed under verification (complete proof: PROOFS.md section 3)
algorithms.space_complexity: O(V): at most 5 n_left + n_right list entries besides the input at any time, also while a list is being replaced (one word per entry; CPython's over-allocation of lists and its integer objects are not counted; PROOFS.md section 10)
algorithms.correctness: Hopcroft & Karp 1973. Augmenting along vertex-disjoint shortest augmenting paths keeps the matching valid, and after a phase that uses a maximal such set, every augmenting path is strictly longer. After phase i every augmenting path has at least 2i + 1 edges. The symmetric difference with a maximum matching contains (maximum - current size) vertex-disjoint augmenting paths, so after sqrt(V) phases at most about sqrt(V)/2 augmentations remain, and every phase performs at least one. Termination when no augmenting path exists gives a maximum matching by Berge's theorem. Complete proof (the BFS layers, the DFS finds a maximal set of vertex-disjoint shortest augmenting paths, the length increase, the phase bound): PROOFS.md section 7.

relationship: O(V E) -> O(E sqrt(V)) (for E = Omega(V)); on dense graphs O(V^3) -> O(V^2.5) (PROOFS.md sections 8-9). Kuhn may traverse the whole graph to find each augmenting path. Hopcroft-Karp finds many shortest augmenting paths per graph traversal, and the shortest-path length must grow every phase.

verification.method: V1: both implementations agree with each other and with an independent algebraic oracle (rank over GF(2^61 - 1) of the Edmonds matrix with random entries, in harness.py; Schwartz-Zippel bounds its error by 10^-15 per instance) on random bipartite graphs (densities 0.05-0.8, balanced and unbalanced sides), complete bipartite graphs, perfect matchings with noise, graphs with isolated vertices and members of the adversarial family, n = 0..10, 18, 20, 39, 50, 68, 100, 200, 300. V2 (since 2026-10-07, research/2026-10-07b_count_based_v2.md) on the adversarial family G_k (n = V = 4k^2 + k, E = 2k^4 + k^2, see harness.py): the measured quantity is the exact number of EDGE SCANS (adjacency-list entries read) by the unchanged implementations, counted by an instrumented adjacency-list type (CountingNeighbours in harness.py, which counts indexing and iteration). These counts equal, value for value, those of the instrumented copies in experiments/2026-10-07_bipartite_matching_counts.py for every k used. Kuhn, k = 3..11: 987, 5190, 19210, 56439, 140945, 312092, 630000, 1181845, 2088999 scans (0.1431-0.1480 V E); alpha = 1.005 against n^3. Hopcroft-Karp, k = 4..15: 4572, 13602, 33313, 71227, 137782, 246812, 416027, 667493, 1028112, 1530102, 2211477, 3116527 scans (1.0153-1.0501 E sqrt V, exactly k + 1 phases); alpha = 1.004 against n^2.5. Tolerance 0.03: exact counts carry no timing noise, so the band only covers lower-order terms (on G_k the ratios scans / n^3 and scans / n^2.5 are not exactly constant, since E = 2k^4 + k^2 is only asymptotically V^2 / 8; largest |alpha - 1| here 0.005) and stays below half the distance to every rival. Rivals that must NOT fit, all rejected: Kuhn against n^2.5 (alpha = 1.207); Hopcroft-Karp against n^2 (1.255) and n^3 (0.837). The validator's log-factor diagnostic is resolved for both (Kuhn 0.941 / 1.079, Hopcroft-Karp 0.936 / 1.083). The earlier timing fit at tolerance 0.25 also passed against the wrong exponents (in experiments/2026-10-07_bipartite_matching_probe.py Kuhn against n^2.5, alpha = 1.168, and Hopcroft-Karp against n^2 and n^3, alpha = 1.221 and 0.815; RESEARCH_LOG RL-030); the exact counts remove that ambiguity. experiments/2026-10-07b_count_v2_matching.py reproduces every count above. Proofs: PROOFS.md proves every claim of this entry from the code (the exact counts on their domains, correctness of both algorithms, the O(sqrt(V)) phase bound, the time and space bounds, the separation over all V, the oracle's error bound and the flow remark) and names the deterministic checks of each, among them tests/test_proofs_matching.py.

caveats: Both bounds are worst-case bounds, and the timing family is adversarial and implementation-specific: a dense K_{2a,a} gadget whose a unmatchable left vertices make each of the a failing Kuhn searches read the lists of its root and of all a matched gadget vertices (a(a + 1) of the gadget's 2a^2 entries), and every Hopcroft-Karp phase read all 2a^2 entries in its breadth-first search, plus paths P_2..P_2k whose adjacency order makes Hopcroft-Karp's first phase choose the wrong edges, so that phase j repairs only path j. The exact counts hold for the adjacency order that harness.adversarial(k) builds. On the 8 random bipartite graphs measured (one each for V = 100, 200, 400, 800 and p = 0.05, 0.5; experiments/2026-10-07_bipartite_matching_counts.py) Hopcroft-Karp needed only 2 to 5 phases, so these graphs do not exhibit its sqrt(V) factor. Kuhn did take about 0.08 V E edge scans on dense random graphs (p = 0.5) and 0.025-0.047 V E on sparse ones (p = 0.05). Over graphs with V vertices the worst cases are Theta(V^3) for Kuhn (at most V E = O(V^3) edge scans on every input, attained up to a constant factor on G_k, and for every V >= 5 on G_k padded with isolated vertices; PROOFS.md section 9) versus O(V^2.5) for Hopcroft-Karp; for sparse graphs only the upper bounds O(V E) and O((V + E) sqrt V) are stated here, without matching lower-bound families. The oracle is randomized (one-sided: a random substitution can only lower the rank), with failure probability below 10^-15 per instance and a deterministic seed (PROOFS.md section 11).
notes: The matchings of size k are exactly the integral flows of value k in the unit-capacity network s -> left -> right -> t, so maximum bipartite matching is the integral maximum-flow problem on that network (PROOFS.md section 12; compare pairs/max-flow-edmonds-karp-vs-dinic).
